'''Silver Ore''' is a raw metal that can be mined from [[Silver Vein]]s found in [[Mountain]] biomes above 120 meters using an [[Iron Pickaxe]] or better. The ore can be smelted into [[Silver]] using a [[Smelter]].

== Availability ==
Silver Veins can be found using the [[Wishbone]] obtained from [[Bonemass]].

Alternatively, hitting the ground with the [[Stagbreaker]] or the [[Wooden Sledge]] may reveal underground silver deposits through the "too hard" message that appears when a silver vein is in the damage area of the two-handed club.

Trenching your positions may inadvertently reveal silver veins, provided you are above 120 meters in elevation. Despite the ground appearing frozen, it is no more difficult to dig in the Mountains than in other biomes, so hitting a vein by sheer luck is not out of the question.

== Notes ==
* Like other metals, Silver Ore cannot be teleported without a [[Portal Stone]].
* If Drakes and Obsidian (100 meters for both) are spawning near the player, they are close to the height needed (120 meters) for Silver to spawn.
* [[Cart]]s may be difficult to use in the Mountains due to the slopes but can be useful to help reduce further trips.
* Silver ore is the heaviest ore of all the ore types.
* Silver Veins cannot be mined by [[Stone Golem]]s or using an [[Antler Pickaxe]].

[[Resin]]|image1=[[fir large.png]]}} Fir is a type of tree that can be found in the [[Black Forest]], [[Swamp]], and [[Mountain]] biomes. It is characterized by its dark brown trunk and long pointed branches. Fir can be found in small and large variants. Both variants can be chopped with a [[Stone Axe]] or better. The small variant produces 4 [[Wood]] when destroyed. The large variant produces 20 [[wood]] when destroyed, and the stump will yield another 2 wood. Fir will sometimes produce a [[Fir Cone]] when destroyed, which can be planted using the [[Cultivator]]. Cutting down a fir tree leaves a stump which is too low to be struck by the regular blow of the axe. To remove stumps, the player must use the alternate attack, which chops straight downward. {| class="wikitable" |+Tree: 50% chance for 1-2 drops !Item !Amount !Chance !Average |- |[[Wood]] |20 |From logs |20 |- |[[Wood]] |2 |From stump |2 |- |[[Fir Cone]] |1 |67% |0.5 |- |[[Feathers]] |1 |17% |0.13 |- |[[Resin]] |1 |17% |0.13 |} {| class="wikitable" |+Small tree ([[Black Forest]], [[Mountain]]): 4-5 drops !Item !Amount !Chance !Average |- |[[Wood]] |1 |83% |3.75 |- |[[Fir Cone]] |1 |8% |0.37 |- |[[Resin]] |1 |8% |0.37 |} {| class="wikitable" |+Small tree ([[Swamp]]): 4-5 drops !Item !Amount !Chance !Average |- |[[Wood]] |1 |100% |4.5 |} ===Planting Firs=== {| class="wikitable" |+Allowed Biomes: !Meadows !Yes |- !Black Forest !Yes |- |Swamp |No |- !Mountain !Yes |- !Plains !Yes |- |Mistlands |No |- |Ashlands |No |} {{Trees}} [[Category:Trees]] [[fr:Sapin]] [[ru:Пихта]] [[cs:Jedle]]

silvervein_frac | location = [[Mountain]] | durability = 40 | tool tier = 2 | resistances = pickaxe only }} '''Silver Veins''' are resource nodes found in tall [[Mountain|Mountains]]. They drop [[Silver Ore]] and [[Stone]] when mined with an [[Iron Pickaxe]] or better. Veins can be detected by equipping the [[Wishbone]]. The Wishbone will emit a tone along with colored particles from the player when a vein is nearby. The tone becomes higher-pitched and faster the closer the player is to the vein. Alternatively, the player can hit the terrain at random positions with [[Stagbreaker]] or an [[Iron Sledge]] until a "Too hard" message is seen under the ground, this is known as [[How to play#How_to_prospect_properly?|Prospecting]]. [[Stagbreaker]] is much more accurate than [[Iron Sledge]] for locating silver in the [[Mountain|Mountains]]. While slower, this does not require killing [[Bonemass]]. == Spawning == The world generator attempts 50 times to find a suitable position for a single vein on every [[Zones|zone]]. The spawn position must have the following conditions: * [[Mountain]] biome * At least 120 meter altitude * Up to 30 degree terrain angle * 10 random points within nine meters have up to a three-meter altitude difference If successful, the vein is placed four meters under the ground. == Drops == Silver Veins always have the same Y-shaped layout with 100 nodes with 40 HP each. Each of the nodes may drop: {{loot table| {{loot row|item=Silver Ore|amt=2-3|rate=33.3%}} {{loot row|item=Stone|amt=2-3|rate=66.7%}} }} On average, one silver vein will produce about 83.3 silver ore and about 166.7 stone. == Notes == * Metal deposits do not respawn. * Like other metals, silver ore cannot be teleported. * Silver Veins sometimes intersect with nearby stone, but can be mined after the stone is removed. * [[Drake]]s and [[obsidian]] require 100 meter altitude to spawn. These can be used to measure the mountain height. * Veins are more likely to appear completely underground on even terrain. However, the random check allows them also to be placed on uneven terrain, which can leave them naturally exposed. * Veins can be mined instantly by removing all supporting ground and then mining a single node. Once the first node breaks all others will follow. This will give all resources instantly but will not give additional [[Pickaxes (Skill)|Pickaxes]] experience. == Gallery == 20210316141925 1.jpg|A silver vein Silver Ore.jpg ValheimSilverVein.jpg 20210325185903 1.jpg|Two silver veins overlapping 20210326202204 1.jpg|A silver vein naturally protruding from the ground SilverVein.png 3.png|Three connected silver ore veins {{WorldNav}} [[cs:Ložisko stříbra]] [[ru:Залежи серебра]]

An '''Obsidian Deposit''' is a resource node and is found in the [[Mountain]]s biome and require an [[Iron Pickaxe]] or better to harvest.

== Availability ==
Obsidian Deposits appear as small, sphere-shaped rocks with distinct black colored veins, which help differentiate them from regular rocks at a distance. They yield [[Obsidian]] when mined.

They are only found on the surface.

== Drops ==
{{loot table|
{{loot row|item=Obsidian|amt=5-8|rate=100%}}
}}

== Notes ==
* Obsidian Deposits do not respawn.
* Unlike other resources that require mining, Obsidian can be teleported.

The '''Eitr Refinery''' is a structure used for processing {{Item Link|Sap}} and {{Item Link|Soft Tissue}} into {{Item Link|Refined Eitr}}.

== Building ==
Eitr Refinery is unlocked once the player has the required materials. A [[Black Metal Axe]] is required to obtain [[Yggdrasil Wood]], and a [[Sap Extractor]] is required to obtain [[Sap]]. The sap extractor requires a [[Dvergr Extractor]] obtained from [[Dvergr Component Crate]]s in Dvergr settlements. [[Infested Mine]]s must also be explored to obtain [[Black Core]]s.

Eitr Refineries can be constructed on flat terrain or on stone floors, but degrade from rain when not under a roof.

== Usage ==
Up to 20 [[Sap]] can be supplied into the funnel at the front of the refinery, and up to 20 [[Soft Tissue]] can be inserted into the grinder at the top. It is possible to climb to the top of the grinder, but constructing stairs makes accessing it easier. The resulting [[Refined Eitr]] is ejected from the tube next to the sap input, opposite the grinder.

The sap:soft tissue ratio is roughly 20:20. Each sap (acting as a fuel) adds 40 seconds, and the operating time on a full fuel tank is 800 seconds. But filling both the Sap and Soft tissue slots to the max will consume 20 Soft tissue and 19 Sap to produce 20 Refined eitr, leaving 1 Sap (probably due to a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-off_error round-off error]).

While processing, small discharges are emitted from the structure, inflicting Lightning and Poison [[Damage]] over time. The eitr dropped on the ground will also emit these discharges, which will eventually damage and destroy structures not immune to elemental damage. Structures immune to elemental damage include [[Cage Wall 2x2|iron]] and [[Dvergr metal wall|copper]] cage pieces, and [[Black Marble]] floor/wall/pillars. Wood and ordinary stone structures will take damage. 

== Notes ==
* As with other [[Mistlands]]-tier structures and items, this can theoretically be obtained before building a [[Wisp Fountain]], but navigation is made difficult by the intense mist.

The '''Sap Extractor''' is a structure used to harvest {{Item link|Sap}} from [[Ancient Roots]] in the [[Mistlands]] [[Biomes|biome]].

==Building==
Sap Extractors can be built on Ancient Roots within the range of a [[Workbench]].

It requires [[Black Metal]], [[Yggdrasil Wood]] and a [[Dvergr Extractor]], obtained from [[Dvergr Component Crate]]s.

==Usage==
When placed on [[Ancient Roots]], the Sap Extractor will extract {{Item link|Sap|1}} from the root every 60 seconds. It can hold a maximum of 10 Sap and glows green if it contains any Sap to harvest. As it is extracting, green particles will leave the top and bottom of the extractor. The particles will stop appearing at the top once the extractor is full, or if attempting to extract from a completely dried root.

As Ancient Roots regenerate Sap much slower than it is extracted, at 1 sap per {{duration|400}} (see their page for details). It is strategic to relocate extractors between multiple roots. Destroying or deconstructing an extractor with Sap inside does not drop the Sap.

==Tips==
* The required Black Metal cannot easily be teleported to the extraction site:
** Therefore, it is advisable to transport some by [[Boat]] before setting off to explore the Mistlands. Ideally, scout the biome for a location with many Ancient Roots as well as tillable ground in proximity, and if so, carry over the Black Metal and set up an outpost.
** Alternatively, the Mistlands biome are generally close to the [[Plains]], so it is possible to acquire [[Black Metal Scrap]] on site. The [[Iron]] needed to build a [[Blast Furnace]] can be mined from [[Ancient Sword]] or [[Ancient Armor]]. All other materials can be teleported via [[Portal]].

'''Ancient Roots''' are a resource found in the [[Mistlands]] biome. [[Sap Extractor]]s can be placed on them to harvest [[Sap]].

==Availability==
Ancient Roots can be commonly found in Mistlands, at ground level. They emit a green light glow which can be seen through the mist.

== Sap harvesting==
Each root dries up as [[Sap]] is extracted from it using a [[Sap Extractor]]. Each Sap Extractor collects and stores one sap every 60 seconds. Multiple sap extractors can be placed on one Ancient Root.

The reservoir of sap in an ancient root regenerates at a rate of 1 sap per {{duration|400}}, up to a maximum storage of 50 sap (obtained in {{duration|20000}}). Thus, sap is a renewable resource. 

Ancient Roots have three visual states: Full, half dried, and dried up.

However, doing so can be dangerous, since the structures that the Dvergr Component Crate is found at are home to [[Dvergr Rogue]]s and/or [[Dvergr Mage]]s, who will turn hostile if the crate (or any other structure under protection of their [[Ward]]s) is damaged directly by a player. The crate can be safely damaged indirectly, or by non-player sources, without angering the Dvergr. == Location == Each of the following structures may hold a Dvergr component crate: * [[Dvergr Guard Tower]] * [[Dvergr Lighthouse]] * [[Dvergr Excavation Site]] * [[Dvergr Harbour]] Note that some of these structures are not guaranteed to contain a component crate. '''Unstable Lava Rocks''' are resource nodes found in the [[Ashlands]] biome, being a source of {{Item link|Proustite Powder}}.

When destroyed by receiving 50 or more damage from any weapon or a [[pickaxe]], they explode. The explosion damages surrounding objects, including players, creatures and structures. Additionally, it creates a small crater in the ground.

== Availability ==
Unstable Lava Rocks can often be found attached to large boulders and stones in the [[Ashlands]] biome, as well as on the ground occasionally.

== Drops ==
{{loot table|
{{loot row|item=Proustite Powder|amt=4-7|rate=100%}}
}}

== Notes ==
* The explosion deals 75 pure damage, regardless of armor rating, and is unblockable. It also deals 500 Chop and 600 Pickaxe damage, but the player is immune to these types of damage.
* The explosion has a tool tier of 4, one higher than Black metal.
* Unstable Lava Rocks can be safely destroyed by shooting them with a [[bow]] or [[crossbows|crossbow]]. [[Frost Arrow]]s are particularly efficient.
